comments.author: rapsoid616
comments.body: I would suggest for you to use some form of auto aim when using those thin poles to grapple. With high speed they would require too much aim skill which I doubt many people that want to play this genre has.

replies.author: _VirtualCosmos_
replies.body:
one suggestion, now that I look at it again. In trackmania one super cool and addictive thing was the near infinite acceleration that promoted the player to press the W the longer possible while risking eating the next curve, making the skill curve very high (one must be very precise with the timings to achieve the fastest loop).

I think having a constant acceleration that the player must regulate add positive vibes to the gameplay as well (tho there must be a maximum speed selected to avoid clipping and bugs like that).

comments.author: VaquinhaAlpha
comments.body:
The idea is really cool! Agree with the comments about the arms looking weird.

Just curious: will this also have all kinds of physics mechanics Trackmania has? With drag, different surfaces friction and all that stuff? I'm not a Trackmania player but I do watch some Wirtual vids here and there and I enjoy the complexity

replies.author: kounaille
replies.body:
Thanks! And yes, the arms are on my list, I’m looking into what I can do there.

For the physics, honestly I haven’t decided yet which direction to go. Either lean fully into the Trackmania side, with time attack, scoring and lots of speed mechanics (and then things like different surface friction would be really interesting), or go more toward multiplayer races like SpeedRunners, racing each other and messing with your opponents. I’m still kind of torn between the two!

replies.author: VaquinhaAlpha
replies.body:
I think the latter probably sells more (as a kind of "party game"), but personally I think you should make the game you want to play

I'm building a game too and it's a kinda niche genre but it's what I've always wanted to see in the industry so I'm doing it, that's my philosophy :p

comments.author: Alarming_Scientist
comments.body: Looks great. What engine was this made in? I'm assuming godot?

replies.author: kounaille
replies.body: Thanks! It's actually Godot 4, built with Claude 🙂

replies.author: Alarming_Scientist
replies.body: How'd you handle animations?

replies.author: kounaille
replies.body: Claude makes a first pass on each animation, then we use a small in-house tool (a pose editor that runs in the browser, kind of like a mini Blender) where I set the key poses myself. Claude then generates the in-between frames and adapts them to the game. For now that's how we move fast on the prototype, but if I push the concept further, I'll probably make it more professional later on 🙂
